question: How much does replacing PVDF with PVDF latex and CMC raise the solids content of NMC 532 slurries, and by what share does the higher solids content cut the primary drying time of the graphite coating?

trace.query: SELECT id, page, text, strength FROM atoms WHERE regexp_matches(lower(text), 'dry|drying|solids|wt%|wt %') ORDER BY page, id

SELECT id, page, text FROM lines WHERE page=8 AND line_no BETWEEN 1 AND 60 OR (page=8 AND id IN ('p8.L24','p8.L27','p8.L32','p8.L33','p8.L34','p8.L35','p8.L36','p8.L37','p8.L38','p8.L39','p8.L40','p8.L41')) ORDER BY id

WITH v AS (
SELECT CAST(regexp_extract((SELECT text FROM atoms WHERE id='p8.L34'), 'from (\d+)', 1) AS DOUBLE) AS t_before,
       CAST(regexp_extract((SELECT text FROM atoms WHERE id='p8.L35'), 'to (\d+) s', 1) AS DOUBLE) AS t_after,
       CAST(regexp_extract((SELECT text FROM atoms WHERE id='p8.L31'), '(\d+)', 1) AS DOUBLE) AS dummy
)
SELECT ROUND(100*(t_before - t_after)/t_before, 1) AS pct_cut, t_before, t_after FROM v

rendered: Replacing PVDF with PVDF latex and CMC raises the solids content of the slurries for NMC 532[1] from 45 wt% to 65 wt%[2], without increasing the slurry viscosity. That is an increase of 20[3] percentage points in solids content. The higher solids content shortens the primary drying time for a graphite coating with a loading of 10 mg/cm^2[4], from from 51[5] s to 34 s[6]. That is a cut of 33.3[7] percent in the primary drying time.
